explanation: The bubble works like a gill: oxygen seeps in from the water and carbon dioxide seeps out, so the spider rarely has to surface to refresh it. It lives in European and Asian ponds.

claims.text: The diving bell spider (Argyroneta aquatica) lives almost entirely underwater, breathing from an air bubble held in a silk web.
Wolf spiders, huntsman spiders and jumping spiders do not live underwater.
The diving bell spider's air bubble acts as a physical gill, taking in oxygen from the water and losing carbon dioxide to it.
Diving bell spiders live in ponds and slow waters in Europe and northern Asia.
